newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas link boosts AmEx sales 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas link boosts AmEx sales 30 pct.

text.p: American Express Co's Australasian and South Pacific unit said on Monday its link with Qantas Airways Ltd's frequent flier programme had boosted sales through American Express cards by 30 percent a year.

"The spend lift has been 30 percent annually and it's been sustained at those levels all the way through," American Express' senior vice president for Australia, New Zealand/South Pacific, John Schaap, said in an address to the Institute of Chartered Accountants.

American Express has a membership rewards programme in Australia and New Zealand where each dollar spent earns a point in either Qantas' frequent flier programme or Air New Zealand Ltd's programme, regardless of where each dollar is spent. The programme was started three years ago.
Schaap said the programme had also increased the percentage of card-holders paying on time and had reduced the attrition or churn rates for American Express.
It had also been a factor in increasing the percentage of people who actually used their American Express card from about 25-30 percent to 63 percent.
Schaap later told reporters the extra sales growth had generated earnings in excess of the cost of the frequent flier programme.

"The liabilities that we've got in our books for that spend lift is less than the spend lift value. There's a cost associated with a loyalty programme, but it is less than the growth than we're getting," he said.
